production.note: US model year 2021 only for the coupe, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): the 2021 listing has one trim, "Coupe 2D", "755 @ 7500 RPM"; KBB's 2022 765LT lists only the "765LT Spider Convertible 2D" (kbb-765lt-2022). McLaren's release (3 March 2020): "Just 765 individually numbered cars available globally to customer order", deliveries from September 2020 (mclaren-765lt-release). The 765LT Spider is sold under its own name.

transmission.note: "7 Speed SSG. Comfort, Sport and Track modes" (McLaren Seamless Shift Gearbox, recorded as a DCT as in the 720S and 600LT records). No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (McLaren 765LT Coupé press release, specification table): "Power PS (bhp/kW) @ rpm | 765 (755/563) @ 7,500rpm". powerStandard is DIN PS because McLaren's rating is the metric 765 PS; 765 x 0.98632 = 755 hp, the bhp figure McLaren prints. KBB's 2021 listing gives the same "755 @ 7500 RPM". The document is McLaren's global release, not a US-specific version.

weightLb.note: Coupe, 7-speed SSG (the only transmission). Quote (McLaren release, specification table): "DIN kerbweight, kg (lbs) [fluids + 90% fuel] | 1,339 (2,952)"; text: "80kg less than 720S coupé at 1,339kg (DIN weight) and just 1,229kg at lightest dry weight". DIN weight, not EU. The row carries no footnote about optional equipment, though standard equipment is light ("no audio system in the standard specification"; "standard lightweight, carbon fibre-shelled racing seats"). McLaren's "Lightest dry weight" of 1,229 kg ("Adopting every weight-saving measure available") depends on options and is not used.
